limitations: Liquid-fraction flow and composition remain provisional.
Storage-tank flow can fall below the validated BioSTEAM cost-correlation range.
Lumped organics, proteins, solids, nutrients, and contaminants are not unique molecular species.
The active thermo does not solve rigorous electrolyte activities or charge balance.
PFAS, pesticides, microplastics, pathogens, and heavy metals are aggregate pools.
PEF release and juice-yield enhancement are empirical.
Press and centrifuge component recoveries are fixed allocations.
No transfer pump is active.
Custom front-end equipment has no approved cost correlation.
Monthly operation is represented by independent steady states.
Protein solubility and effective isoelectric pH are aggregate approximations.
Acid demand lacks project titration data.
Precipitation and heat-coagulation kinetics are not calibrated.
Co-precipitation and protein capture use component-specific fixed fractions.
Cake washing and dewatering are single-stage empirical allocations.
Dryer kinetics, air humidity, area, and heat recovery are not modelled.
Neutralized-liquid pH and salt effects are not rigorous electrolyte predictions.
No approved custom-equipment CAPEX correlations are available.
Protein product quality and regulatory suitability are undetermined.
Digester-feed pH conditioning is not solved from buffering chemistry.
Hydrolysis uses fixed component-group conversions.
Acidogenesis, acetogenesis, and methanogenesis are fixed ultimate-fate stages rather than dynamic populations.
Pseudo-component digestion is balanced on mass, COD, C, N, P, and S rather than full molecular H/O stoichiometry.
One combined anaerobic biomass pool represents all microbial populations.
Free-ammonia, VFA, and salinity inhibition are disabled.
Gas-liquid partitioning uses empirical Level-1 fractions.
H2S and inorganic-carbon speciation are screening-level and not charge-balanced.
Raw-biogas water vapour uses a specified wet-mole fraction rather than saturation.
Digester heat loss uses a lumped U-value and conceptual geometry.
Mixing power is a volume-based placeholder.
Equalization dynamics, pumping, and recycle loops are not active.
Two-stage and high-rate digesters are inactive.
Persistent contaminants are conserved and pathogen reduction is not claimed.
No digester, gas-holder, or custom-separator CAPEX is assigned.
The digester is steady-state and has no startup, upset, or automatic control simulation.
Raw biogas and digestate have no product or regulatory classification.
Biogas cooling uses pure-water saturation pressure and ideal-gas humidity.
Condensate-separator geometry is residence-time based.
H2S removal and media replacement use class-E removal and capacity values.
Iron-sponge hydration and biological kinetics are not represented.
Ammonia washing does not solve pH-dependent gas-liquid equilibrium.
Siloxanes are represented by one D5-equivalent marker and empirical capture.
Water scrubbing uses a calibrated apparent-partition model.
Gas drying uses bounded water-removal fractions.
Membrane permeances and area are class-E structural values.
PSA is a Level-1 cycle-average allocation rather than a dynamic bed model.
MEA absorption uses equivalent loading rather than rigorous electrolyte chemistry.
MEA regeneration heat is a specific-energy placeholder.
MEA degradation is one elemental-equivalent pool.
No custom gas-cleaning or upgrading CAPEX correlation is approved.
Feed and product quality limits are structural checks rather than selected end-use standards.
CHP and cryogenic scenarios remain inactive data-gated architectures.
Plant-wide CHP, heat recovery, biomethane storage/compression, and grid injection are not yet implemented.
Raw-gas trace contaminants are absent unless measured upstream values exist.
Digestate equalization is a monthly steady-state vessel, not a dynamic buffer.
Digestate separation is a component-class capture and cake-moisture model.
Struvite precipitation does not solve electrolyte activities, charge balance, or Ksp.
Struvite nucleation and crystal-growth kinetics are not modelled.
Calcium-phosphate recovery selects one ideal bookkeeping formula.
Crystal recovery, impurity capture, and product moisture are empirical.
Target pH does not calculate base demand from alkalinity.
Digestate heating uses a constant bulk heat capacity and no exchanger design.
Ammonia stripping uses a monotonic NTU-like response rather than a rate-based column.
Carbonate and ammonia acid-base chemistry are not rigorously re-equilibrated.
Acid capture is stoichiometric but absorber hydraulics and product concentration are structural.
Ion exchange is a cycle-average site-equivalent recycle, not dynamic breakthrough.
Evaporation does not solve salt solubility or scaling precipitation.
Membrane concentration uses class-specific rejection coefficients.
Product storage is an uncosted hold-up interface.
Optional washing and drying use empirical displacement and bulk moisture equations.
No custom Phase 7 equipment CAPEX is assigned.
The repository has no active BG1 CHP or plant-wide utility network.
Contaminant pools are conserved but product-specific partitioning is mostly physical entrainment.
Unspeciated dissolved-P and particulate-P pools are not assumed precipitable.
Months are independent steady states and equipment uses peak-month scaling.
Whole-digestate phosphorus recovery uses the same Level-1 chemistry as centrate treatment.
Reported nutrient streams are not certified fertilizers or reusable water.

maturity_summary.interpretation: Counts describe evidence and completeness only; they are not a validation score or TRL estimate.

climate.definition: Attributional plant climate estimate; partial inventory may be used for screening and must be completed before investment decisions

net_carbon.definition: Operational climate load converted from t CO2e to t C, less assumed carbon stored in furniture and soil-retained nutrient-rich solids; screening proxy.

npv.definition: After-tax constant-account screening cash flows; explicit CAPEX override where provided, upfront grant, user-rated labor/utilities/logistics, product sales, and time-limited operating support; working capital recovered at end of project.

operating_profit.definition: Original modeled annual sales minus partial OPEX, before support, tax and capital recovery; no assumed performance improvements.

route_trl.definition: No evidence-backed route-level TRL aggregation exists; never inferred from component maturity

subsidy_granted.definition: Present value of the assumed upfront CAPEX grant plus discounted operating-support overlay; the Pareto analysis computes the overlay dynamically from candidate biomethane volume, not as a fixed €/t-feed rate. This is not an eligibility or award estimate.
